column1: # .github/secret-reveal-allow.tsv — every place a secret.Value's bytes leave
# api/cmd/secretlint reports every selection of secret.Value.Reveal (SL01)
# and fails on one this file does not name. A row is a reviewed site: the
# reason says why the bytes must leave there. The gate also fails on a row
# that matches no site, so a row cannot outlive its code.
# SL02 (unsafe or reflect access to a type that holds a secret.Value) has no
# allowlist: there is no row that admits one.
# A row is keyed on path + enclosing symbol, never on a line number — the
# Checked by: go run ./api/cmd/secretlint <one ./module/... per go.work module>

column3: Checks the key's length and that it is not all zeroes, and copies it into the session's own payload (secret.New), so the handler's Destroy cannot reach the session.
Copies the session's key into the stream grant's own payload under the lock, so a session closing mid-stream cannot zero the bytes an unseal is reading.
Derives the public key from the private key to prove it opens the claimed target; the X25519 derivation takes bytes.
Unseals the identity archive far enough to read the trusted manifest; Unseal takes the key as bytes.
Unseals one member into the restore stream; Unseal takes the key as bytes. The grant's copy is destroyed when the handler returns.
